title: How to avoid buying stolen Nintendo Switch 2 consoles - NewsBreak
text: DENVER (KDVR) — The investigation continues into the theft of more than a million dollars’ worth of Nintendo Switch 2 video game consoles stolen from a Bennett truck stop. The Arapahoe County Sheriff’s office says 2,810 consoles were stolen from the delivery truck on June 8. There are concerns that the stolen goods may end up for sale on online marketplaces. Check Point Software Global Channel Leader in the Office of the CTO, Dave Meister, tells FOX31 anyone looking to buy the consoles should be cautious. “I think Facebook Marketplace is probably one of the most common, you do still see a lot coming through on eBay as well,” he said. FOX31 found some eBay sellers are charging hundreds more for the consoles, but Meister says beware of unusually cheap deals. “If somebody’s selling it again at 30, 40% lower, but it’s not through a reputable site like Best Buy or through the manufacturer’s website, then it’s probably not going to be legitimate,” he said. High-pressure sales tactics are another red flag; be wary of anyone who reaches out to you directly to sell a unit. Meister advises that anyone looking to purchase an item check out the seller by doing a Google image search. “Utilize things like Google images to do a reverse lookup to actually look at people’s profiles start to look at the background of who are they connected with, have they posted anything previously, looking at these types of indicators are generally going to give you a good understanding of whether they are legitimate or not,” he said. Serial numbers on stolen items are usually tracked. Buyers should ask to see the number and inquire with Nintendo about whether the number matches any stolen merchandise. The number is located on the bottom of the console. Anyone who thinks a console is stolen should contact the Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to FOX31 Denver.
